item.title: Welcome to learning-materials
item.description: This site runs on HAXcms with a custom theme that brings the features of the learning-materials-decapcms platform to HAX: content types with fields, pathways, versions, books, embedding and open licensing, plus an editor redesigned in the shadcn/ui style. This page explains what is new and where to find it. item.title: Animation Principles
item.description: Learn the twelve principles of animation and how to apply them to create believable movement in 3D animation. Master the fundamental principles of animation that bring characters and objects to life through believable movement and performance.

item.title: Lessons
item.description: Lessons group lectures, tutorials and exercises around a set of learning objectives.

item.title: Animating a bouncing ball
item.description: In this exercise, level 1 students will practice keyframe animation to animate a bouncing ball Learning Objectives Practice keyframe animation of translation, rotation, and scale properties. Become familiarized with keyframe animation. Apply principles of animation Instructions Watch linked tutorials in Learning Resources to get acquainted with animation tools. item.title: Animated textures
item.description: In this exercise, you will apply an image sequence as texture object in Blender, render a final Blender animation as an image sequence, and import it into after effects. You will create a compressed video in a web streaming format called H.264. Learning Objectives Become familiarized with adding animation sequences as moving textures on 3D geometry. item.description: Formative practice focused on a narrow set of competencies.

item.title: Pathways
item.description: A pathway is one run of a course, 6 or 15 weeks, shaped around what you want to do in 3D. Everyone starts with CGI Foundations; after that, choose a pathway, and take it again at a higher level on a repeat run.

item.title: History of CGI
item.description: An introduction to the history and evolution of computer-generated imagery, exploring how CGI has transformed visual storytelling and design across multiple industries.

item.title: You don't see that everyday object posters
item.description: For this project, you will produce 3D rendered poster series of objects that you encounter every day, but augmented in such a way changing their nature including material qualities, operation or use, or the system or environmental context. To explore these concepts, we delve into the philosophical realm of objects and their existence, considering how we interact with them in both a functional and perceptual sense. item.title: 3D Modeling Fundamentals
item.description: Learn the core principles and techniques of 3D modeling, focusing on polygon modeling methods that form the foundation for all 3D content creation.

item.title: Modeling the Airline Chair
item.description: In this exercise, you will practice polygonal modeling fundamentals and will use 3D software to build a polygonal model of the 1930s Kem Weber Airline Chair. Learning Objectives Practice using 3D software interface and terminology. Use modeling workflows to create high quality topology and edge flow. item.title: Stylized Prop Set
item.description: Design and build a small set of stylized, game-ready props that share a palette and style, and present them in a real-time engine. Learning Objectives Design a cohesive set of props Build each prop within a polygon budget Texture the set with a shared palette Present the set in PlayCanvas

item.title: Texturing and UV Mapping
item.description: Master the art of UV mapping and texturing, learning how to properly unwrap 3D models and apply high-quality textures and materials.

item.title: Modeling a room
item.description: In this exercise, you will practice polygonal modeling fundamentals and will use 3D software to build a polygonal model of an interior space. Learning Objectives Become familiarized with 3D software terminology Practice polygonal modeling workflows Perform fundamental polygonal modeling operations including extrude, merge, bridge, and bevel. Instructions Note: There are no step-by-step tutorials for this intermediate level exercise. See beginner level exercises if you need guided instruction....

item.title: Modular Environment Kit
item.description: Build a kit of modular environment pieces that snap together on a grid, then use it to assemble a small scene. Learning Objectives Plan a modular grid and pivot conventions Model and texture reusable pieces Assemble a scene from the kit in a real-time engine

item.title: Lighting Principles
item.description: Learn the fundamental principles of lighting in 3D, including light types, placement strategies, and techniques for creating compelling visual scenes.

item.title: Realtime Game Environment
item.description: For this project, you will design and build a simple first person real-time 3D game environment that functions not only as a playable space, but as a meaningful spatial experience. In games, environments guide a players movement, establish atmosphere, suggest histories, and communicate how a world is used without relying entirely on dialogue or text.
